source_title: 'Suit spotted on Traitors' and 'air raid shelters found' - BBC
source_excerpt:
Here's our weekly round up of stories from across local websites in the West of England.
What have been the big stories in the West this week?
Somerset Council outlined repair plans for Burnham-On-Sea's historic Low Lighthouse amid fresh concerns about its condition.
Four abandoned air raid shelters were discovered under four schools in Bristol this week.
A man with additional needs who mistook Prince William for Prince the pop star and asked him to sing "Purple Rain" has written to the royal to apologise.
Footage of a copper beech tree that was planted on Victoria Square in Clifton Village in 1860 and toppled by Storm Boelo has been shared on social media. It had recently been earmarked for felling because its roots had been infected by a fungus.
And new powers aimed at cracking down on persistent anti-social behaviour have come into force in Weston-super-Mare .
Top five local stories for the BBC in the West
How close are we to running out of water?
Big Ben restorers to fix toppled Jubilee clock
Teacher who drove to pupil's house in night banned
The man who chooses to sleep with bedbugs
Seeing Claudia in my suit was ridiculously exciting
For more than a decade , Bristol City Council and Avon and Somerset Police have been collaborating on mass data gathering programmes used to profile tens of thousands of people in the city – including 55,000 families on the controversial Think Family database and app.
Bristol City Council says its mass data gathering tool is designed to protect, not profile the 55,000 families it monitors.
